One page per source. Each says what the source is, where it comes from, its
licence and how to cite it, how its tables join the rest of the release, and
the caveats worth knowing. The tables, row counts and upstream versions on
every page are read from the latest release's `manifest.json` when the page
loads, so they do not go stale between releases.

## Connect

Every table is a view in `bioconice.duckdb` and a plain Parquet file. In DuckDB
(CLI, R or Python), with no account, token or extension:

```sql
ATTACH 'https://data.bioconice.cancerdatasci.org/latest/bioconice.duckdb' AS bioc (READ_ONLY);
SELECT * FROM bioc.annotation.hgnc__gene LIMIT 5;
```

`latest/` moves with each weekly release; pin a dated folder or a monthly
Hugging Face release for reproducible work, as [Versions and
citation](../guides/versions-and-citation.qmd) explains. From R, the
[`bioconice` package](https://github.com/seandavi/bioconice) wraps the same
connection. The Parquet files are linked from each source's table below, and
any Parquet reader can open them directly.

## The sources

::: {#sources-index}
Loading from the latest release…
:::

Three tables stack rows from several sources and appear on each contributor's
page: `annotation.identifier_mapping` (NCBI Gene, Ensembl, HGNC, MANE,
RNAcentral, UniProt), `annotation.interaction` (BioGRID, IntAct) and
`resource.resource_relationship` (BEDbase, CELLxGENE, ENCODE, eQTL Catalogue).
Each row names its writer in a `source` column. `provenance.release` records,
per release and source, the upstream version, URL and retrieval time every
table was built from.
